entry.title: Moorings passes 1,000 bookings a month
entry.content: In February, visiting boats made 1,042 bookings through Moorings. Most came from harbours that joined last summer. The thing that did not work: paid ads. Every harbour came from a recommendation.
entry.summary: The numbers, what worked, and the one thing that did not.

entry.title: The harbour at low tide: what a slow month taught us

link.title: The harbour at low tide: what a slow month taught us

entry.content: When the harbour empties, so does our booking calendar. This January we fixed eighty small bugs, rewrote the welcome email, and took a week off.
entry.summary: January is our quietest month. This year we used it to fix everything we had put off.

entry.title: Keeping a commonplace book of customer calls

link.title: Keeping a commonplace book of customer calls

entry.content:
A commonplace book is a notebook of things worth keeping. Mine is every customer call since day one.1 Here is how I keep it useful.

The rules

  1. Write the date before anything else.
  2. Copy the source with every note, even a page number.
  3. Never delete an entry; cross it out instead.

Date - first, before the harbour’s name.

Ask - what they asked for, in their words.

A worked example

Harbour Asked for Notes
North Quay refunds built in March
Port Ellery a printed list built in May
Salt Cove dark mode not yet

Your customers will tell you what to build if you write it down.

When the notes moved to a computer I wrote a tiny script to rebuild the index:

2025-03-02  North Quay   refunds        built
2025-05-11  Port Ellery  printed list   built
2025-06-19  Salt Cove    dark mode      open

  1. It is now a spreadsheet, but I still call it the book. ↩
entry.summary: Every call with a harbour master goes into one notebook. Here is the system.

entry.title: We sold the tide tables print shop

link.title: We sold the tide tables print shop

entry.content: The print shop was my first business. It now belongs to the printer down the road, who was doing most of the work anyway.
entry.summary: Five years, four thousand tables, and a happy new owner.

entry.title: Pricing for harbour masters
entry.content: Small harbours are busy for four months a year. A monthly fee would cost them money all winter, so we charge a small fee per booking instead.
entry.summary: Why Moorings charges per booking, not per month.

entry.title: Monthly update: March
entry.content: Twelve harbours joined in March. Refunds are now one click. It rained on twenty-six days.
entry.summary: Twelve new harbours, one new feature, and a lot of rain.

entry.title: Why we do not take investment

link.title: Why we do not take investment

entry.content: Our customers are small and so are we. Growing at their speed keeps us close to them.
entry.summary: A short note on growing slowly on purpose.
